tasks.spec:
You are a repo feature worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repository, detached at HEAD. Edit files here directly.

OWNERSHIP: you own exactly two paths, factory/remote_outbox_pull.py (new) and tests/test_remote_outbox_pull.py (new). Do NOT modify, create, delete, or reformat anything else under factory/, tests/, kernel/, runbooks/, departments/, or loopfactory.py. Do NOT git commit or push, do NOT run git add -A. Leave changes uncommitted; the check exports them.

CONTEXT. Agents run on more than one machine. A second machine (a Mac mini running Codex) raises approval packets by appending JSON lines to its own local outbox file. It deliberately holds NO credential: no Linear token, no Telegram token, no ssh key inbound. This box already has outbound ssh access to that machine, so THIS box pulls the packets down. Once a pulled file lands in the right local path, the existing mailroom turns each new line into a Linear card and a phone buzz. You are building only the pull.

READ FIRST, READ-ONLY: factory/outbox_push.py, especially how it uses a cursor keyed by watch path with an offset and recent row hashes, and factory/human_in_the_loop.py for the atomic-write convention used throughout this repo.

BUILD factory/remote_outbox_pull.py with this CLI:
  python3 factory/remote_outbox_pull.py --source <src> --dest <dest> [--ssh-host <user@host>] [--identity <keyfile>]
Behaviour:
1. When --ssh-host is absent, --source is a plain LOCAL path. This mode is not a toy: it is how the puller is verified without a second machine, and the check uses it.
2. When --ssh-host is present, fetch the remote file over ssh or scp using --identity if supplied. Never read, print, or log the contents of the identity file; pass it to the transport only.
3. APPEND-ONLY MERGE. --dest is the file the mailroom watches. Bring across only lines not already present, preserving order. Pulling twice in a row must add nothing. A new remote line must arrive on the next pull.
4. AN EMPTY SOURCE IS A QUIET SUCCESS, NOT A FAILURE. An outbox with zero lines means nobody has raised anything, which is the normal state most of the time. Exit 0 and report 0 rows added. A previous attempt treated empty as an error, which would turn the timer red on almost every tick and train the operator to ignore it. That is the always-green disease inverted and it is just as dangerous.
5. FAIL CLOSED AND NON-DESTRUCTIVE on real trouble: if the source is unreachable or unreadable, exit nonzero with a printed reason AND leave --dest exactly as it was. Never truncate, never clobber, never write a partial file into place: build the new content and move it into position atomically. Losing a pulled packet loses a decision the owner never got the chance to make.
6. Skip blank lines. A line that is not valid JSON is a real problem: refuse it loudly rather than passing malformed input to the mailroom.
7. Print a one-line summary of how many rows were added, so a timer log is readable.

WRITE tests/test_remote_outbox_pull.py covering local-source pull, idempotency, incremental arrival, EMPTY-source quiet success, unreachable-source non-destruction, and malformed-line refusal. Use tmp_path and the repo's existing subprocess test style. Your tests are not the acceptance gate; an independent oracle drives the CLI through fixtures you have not seen.

VERIFY from the worktree root: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider. The whole suite must stay green.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave the two owned files edited and uncommitted, and write ./notes.md at the ROOT of your worktree recording what you read, what you changed, the exact verification command and its result, and any assumption.

HARD RULES: no new dependencies, no allow-on-failure paths, and no credential ever read or logged. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do not capture anything to any memory or brain service.
tasks.verified: an independent oracle drove the pull-leg CLI through fixtures the worker never saw and the full repo suite still passes; only owned files changed; patch exported outside the worktree.
